title: We visited the Suffolk village known for a UFO mystery and royal history
excerpt: In the latest in the EADT's Village Visit series we are in Rendlesham in east Suffolk filled with ancient history and UFO mystery.
content:
When it comes to Suffolk villages, Rendlesham is arguably more famous than most due to its historic Anglo-Saxon links and the alleged sighting of a certain UFO.

Archaeological discoveries have shown the village was once a major Royal centre of the Angles' kingdom of East Anglia and was believed to be the residence of the East Anglian kings from the Wuffingas dynasty.

The village lies just a few miles from the burial site at Sutton Hoo, where these kings are believed to have been laid to rest and where the historic longship was discovered in 1939 by Basil Brown.

The village church at Rendlesham is a familiar sight in the village (Image: Newsquest)

In more recent times, the United States Air Force (USAF) was based at nearby RAF Bentwaters during the Second World War, before leaving in 1993, with much of the former base housing having been converted for civilian use.

These days the village is home to more than 3,000 residents, who seemed largely contented with life, praising Rendlesham's "community spirit."

Carol Wyard and her daughter Sophie were out walking in the village centre and described how everyone looked out for each other.

Christina Haynes said Rendlesham was a safe place for children (Image: Newsquest)

Sophie said when a villager's dog went missing, "tons of people" responded to an online appeal to help track down the errant pet, searching areas as far afield as Tunstall.

She also highlighted the role staff at the Costcutter store in Rendlesham played in village life, which included providing chocolate eggs for children over the Easter period.

There is also a minifair at Christmas where children can visit Father Christmas, while she was looking forward to a new takeaway diner being developed by the owners of the Costcutter, which will be called Maeme's piri piri.

Ziyad Mohammed, who runs the Costcutter store, said Rendlesham had one of the strongest community spirits he had ever come across (Image: Newsquest)

"I think it is a nice village to live in. It is surrounded by nature and has nice places to go.

"It has a nice village shop. We have got a Costcutter that we have had for a while and behind it is a Co-Op and there will be a new takeaway, which will be exciting," she added.

Ziyad Mohammed owns the Costcutter and Post Office, which he has run since 2018 and will be developing the new takeaway.

The nearby former RAF Bentwaters has been converted into Base Business Park (Image: Newsquest)

He said: "I love the community spirit here. It is one of the strongest communities I have ever come across in my whole life and since we started with the Costcutter and Post Office, we have been working really closely with the community and helping the community as much as possible."

Mother and daughter Carol and Sophie Wyard said the village was a nice place to live (Image: Newsquest)

Christina Haynes said: "I have been here for ten years and I love the community spirit and that people come together for all different activities and celebrations.

"I love that it is a very child friendly village. We have got kids and it is very family friendly. I love that it has a safe feeling for children and they can go out and play and not feel like they are in danger."

The village primary school was also praised (Image: Newsquest)

She lauded Rendlesham Social Club and praised Rendlesham Primary School for the support given to children.

As well as the Costcutter, Post Office, Co-Op and primary school, the village also boasts the Church of St Gregory the Great.

Last week, the village also became home to the fifth Honey & Harvey cafe at the Bake Business Park, with a number of people flocking through the door on opening day.

Operations manager Shannon Hammond explained the location enabled Honey and Harvey to bring more of its baking in-house, partly to control costs, while there was also the opportunity of working with other bakers nearby.

The branch is open Monday to Saturday from 8am to 4pm, while six new staff members have been recruited for the new business so far.

The nearby Rendlesham Forest was the site of a famous UFO sighting in December 1980 by USAF airmen and also hosts a regular 5km parkrun every Saturday at 9am.

Rendlesham Forest was the site of a famous alleged UFO sighting (Image: Newsquest)
